<STRUCT_0001>
Given <MATH_0001>, we can ask: if the fibre
category <MATH_0002> is a groupoid for all <MATH_0003>,
must <MATH_0004> be fibred in groupoids over <MATH_0005>? We can see the
answer is no as follows. Start with a category fibred in groupoids
<MATH_0006>. Altering the morphisms in <MATH_0007>
which do not map to the identity morphism on some object does not alter the
categories <MATH_0008>. Hence we can violate the existence and uniqueness
conditions on lifts. One example is the functor from Example
<REF_0001> when <MATH_0009> is not
surjective. Here is another example.
